open_points.subject: R0-14 conflict-copy recognition
open_points.question: By what exact, testable rule does the deliverer distinguish a Syncthing conflict copy from an ordinary file?
options: Read Syncthing metadata or an index
Store conflict status when first discovered
Treat any filename resembling a conflict copy as one
open_points.default_guess: Match the configured Syncthing version's conflict-copy filename pattern on every scan.

witness.initial: The photo folder contains an ordinary user-created file whose name resembles a Syncthing conflict-copy name.
events: The deliverer scans the photo folder.
The owner opens the workplace's ready-photo list.
outcomes: The filename rule classifies the file as a conflict copy and excludes it.
A provenance-based rule classifies it as an ordinary photo and offers it.

open_points.subject: R0-14 exclusion presentation
open_points.text: The deliverer does not offer such a copy.
open_points.question: Does the workplace omit the conflict copy entirely, show it as ineligible with a reason, or report it separately?
options: Show it disabled with a conflict-copy reason
Show a separate warning or count
open_points.default_guess: Show it as ineligible with a conflict-copy reason so the owner can discover why it was excluded.

witness.initial: A conflict copy exists under the confirmed photo folder.
outcomes: The conflict copy is absent, so the owner sees no indication that it exists.
The conflict copy is visible but disabled with an explanation.

open_points.subject: R0-14 rename transition
open_points.text: the owner who wants that version renames it, after which it is an ordinary photo
open_points.question: What rename makes the file ordinary, when is that change detected, and does it become offerable subject to the existing content-delivery rule or regardless of prior delivery of identical content?
options: Any path change makes it ordinary immediately
It becomes ordinary only when its new name no longer matches the conflict-copy rule, on the next scan
The owner must explicitly refresh or start a new delivery
Renaming overrides prior content-based delivery history
open_points.default_guess: On the next scan, treat it as ordinary only if its new name no longer matches the conflict-copy rule, while retaining content-based deduplication.

witness.initial: A conflict copy is excluded, and its content is identical to content already recorded as delivered.
events: The owner renames the conflict copy to a normal-looking filename.
The owner opens or refreshes the ready-photo list.
outcomes: Renaming makes it offerable because the passage says it is now an ordinary photo.
Content identity keeps it unoffered because the same content was already delivered.

open_points.subject: R0-14 selection race
open_points.text: The deliverer does not offer such a copy.
open_points.question: Must conflict status be checked again after listing and before placing, and what result is reported if a selected ordinary file becomes a conflict copy before delivery?
options: Revalidate before placing and fail that photo with a conflict-copy reason
Use the classification captured when the ready list was produced
Remove the stale choice without a per-photo result
open_points.default_guess: Revalidate immediately before placing and report that photo as failed with a conflict-copy reason while continuing the others.

witness.initial: An ordinary photo appears in the ready list and the owner selects it.
events: Syncthing turns or replaces the selected path into a conflict copy before execution.
outcomes: The calling flow trusts the earlier list and delivers the conflict copy.
The calling flow revalidates and refuses to place it.
witness.observer: The owner and, if the photo is later shown, the client

open_points.subject: R0-14 existing deliverer state
open_points.text: The deliverer does not offer such a copy.
open_points.question: When R0-14 takes effect, what happens to conflict copies already cached as ready, previously selected, or stored in deliverer records?
options: Reclassify and remove them from readiness immediately
Reclassify them on the next scan
Grandfather existing records until the folder changes
open_points.default_guess: Reclassify all current candidates on the next scan and invalidate any persisted ready or selected entry that is now a conflict copy.

witness.initial: Before R0-14, the deliverer stored a conflict copy as a ready candidate.
events: The owner opens the existing ready list and starts delivery.
outcomes: The stored candidate remains selectable and is delivered.
The candidate is reclassified and is no longer offered.
